title: Getting data in
summary: Everything the runtime ingests arrives at the platform broker as Sparkplug B. Devices that speak it connect directly. Anything else goes through the organization's adapter runtime, where a decoder turns the vendor's payload into profile metrics and a platform-owned publisher announces them as Sparkplug B.

boxes.label: Sparkplug B devices
boxes.detail: Hardware that already publishes Sparkplug B connects to the platform broker over TLS with credentials confined to its organization's group. Nothing translates its messages.

boxes.label: Vendor MQTT devices
boxes.detail: Two source types. With `platform` the hardware publishes to the tenant's ingress broker, using a credential that may only publish to the adapter's topic filters. With `vendor` the adapter subscribes to the manufacturer's broker, which must be publicly reachable.

boxes.label: Vendor cloud webhooks
boxes.sub: HTTPS POST to an ingest URL
boxes.detail: A vendor cloud that pushes data posts to the adapter's ingest URL, `/w/<ingest id>`. Source type `webhook`.

boxes.label: Vendor HTTP API
boxes.detail: A vendor cloud that must be asked. Source type `poll`: the adapter runtime sends the request the settings describe, every 60 seconds to 24 hours, and keeps a cursor. The same child diagram as webhooks shows how.

boxes.label: Platform MQTT broker
boxes.detail: Every path ends here. Each adapter is one Sparkplug edge node, `adapter-<adapter uuid>`, in the organization's group `adapters-<organization uuid>`, with its own broker credentials.

edges.label: Sparkplug B, one edge node per adapter

steps.text: A Sparkplug B gateway or device publishes births and data straight to the platform broker.
Firmware built on the embedded SDK is such a device: the SDK runs the Sparkplug session so the firmware only writes values.
A device with its own MQTT payloads publishes to the tenant's ingress broker, or the adapter subscribes to the vendor's broker.
A vendor cloud posts a webhook. The receiver checks its size, secret and rate limits; a delivery that fails is refused and never reaches a decoder.
An accepted delivery is published to the adapter's topic on the tenant's ingress broker, so it joins the same path as MQTT input.
For a polling source the adapter runtime asks the vendor's API itself and feeds each record to the decoder.
What runs in the tenant runtime is a tested adapter revision that the API deployed through adapter-manager. Nobody edits flows by hand.
The decoder's output is republished as Sparkplug B by a publisher the platform owns. Each physical source becomes a device under the adapter's edge node.
From the broker on, the runtime treats all of it alike. Open telemetry ingest to follow a packet to storage.
